tasks.title: Lane fixture and serial baseline: a sandbox repo with 9 tasks (6 independent, 3 chained by waits_on, 3 editing one shared function), each with a verify command. Serial drive's wall-clock, tasks done, verify pass rate, tokens per task and conflicts are the bar every later step must beat

Load control so lanes do not saturate the machine: a verify semaphore (one full suite at a time), nice/taskpolicy for sessions and verify, process-group kill on verify timeout, a vitest maxWorkers cap (drive-load note 01M3PCDC, fixes 1-5)
Ready frontier: readyTasks honours waits_on (queuedTasks ignores it today, drive-queue.ts:42); `sofar next --ready`; serial drive takes the ready head
Record-root override: a lane session writes the main checkout's .sofar, never its worktree's stale committed copy; lanes never commit .sofar

`sofar drive --lanes N`: a persistent lane worktree pool (deps installed once), tasks as branches, lanes recorded on run_started. `--lanes 1` stays byte-identical to today's run (session-driver D6 holds there)

Coordinator: one process assigns ready tasks to free lanes and records each assignment, so the statusline and interactive sessions see which lane holds which task. Budgets (--cost-cap, --max-sessions) count across lanes; a rate-limited lane parks instead of stalling

Serial merge queue: rebase a passing task branch onto the run base, re-verify when the base moved, fast-forward. A conflict becomes a merge handoff to the lane's next session. Affected-tests verify per merge, full suite per batch

Measure local lanes against serial on the 1.1 fixture. Keep only if wall-clock falls ≥40%, duplicate work is 0, tasks done and verify pass rate are no lower, merge-conflict reopens ≤10% and tokens per task rise ≤5%

Region leases at PreToolUse: an Edit's old_string maps to its markdown section or enclosing symbol, else the whole file. An overlap with another lane stops the edit with a reason; the session works elsewhere or parks (WIP commit, write-back, leases released). Older task wins, so no deadlock; union-merge files never lease. NEEDS the operator's ruling on r4-fixes D17 (deny only on an explicit-forbid rule) for driven lanes

Footprint prediction and conflict-aware scheduling: task `touches`, the record's mention index, files earlier sessions on the task touched, git co-change. A free lane takes the first ready task that misses every live lease and footprint, else idles; skipped tasks age up

Context packets, deterministic and one line each: lease notice (who holds what, for which task), change brief on merge (task, regions, diffstat, decisions and memories logged, write-back), park/resume packet (own write-back, WIP sha, the brief it waited for)
Measure conflict-aware lanes against naive lanes: merge-conflict rework sessions, parks, lanes busy, wall-clock. Keep each piece only if it improves on 2.5

Cloud launch and readback without a TTY: `claude --cloud` refuses a non-TTY (r4-fixes M24). Verify a scriptable launch (routines via API call, or a pty), a branch per task, results back through pushed branches (needs the Claude GitHub App on the repo), and session end detected from the branch's record

Cloud lane adapter: a lane is a cloud session on its task branch. The local coordinator polls and fetches, verifies locally, merges through the queue, and `--resume` re-attaches after the laptop sleeps (the record is the queue)
Conflicts in cloud lanes: no edit-time leases (a cloud VM cannot read the local lease store), so scheduling by footprint plus the merge queue. Measure conflict rework against local lanes
Measure cloud lanes against local lanes: wall-clock, cost per task, tasks finished with the laptop closed, verify pass rate

payload.chose: 1.2 ships five load-control fixes: (1) a verify slot, one gate command at a time per user on the machine; (2) nice 10, plus taskpolicy -c utility on macOS, for sessions and gate commands; (3) gate commands async in their own process group, killed whole on a timeout or an interrupt and swept when the shell exits, with stop requests read while they run; (4) a vitest maxWorkers cap; (5) a timeout retried once before it reopens the task

payload.because: Load is a property of the machine: drives of other initiatives and other repos verify on the same box, and lanes of one coordinator contend on the lock too, since flock is per open file description. The kernel releases the lock however its holder dies, as it does for the run lock. An unattended run must have no state it can sit in forever, and the holder's command is bounded by its own timeout.
payload.chose: The verify slot is per user per machine: a flock-semantics lock on <state base>/verify.lock, on the run lock's primitive, polled so stop requests are still read. The wait is bounded by the command's own timeout, after which the command runs without the slot and a warning says so
payload.over: A per-repo slot under the git common dir; an in-process semaphore in the coordinator; an unbounded blocking wait

payload.because: setPriority races a shell's first fork. -b confines the process to the efficiency cores and throttles its I/O, which would slow every driven test run. An unresolved binary spawned through a wrapper would exit 127 (nice) or 66 (taskpolicy) instead of failing with ENOENT and spawn_error. Library callers include parallel vitest workers that share one hermetic state base, and a default-on slot would serialize their verifications.
payload.chose: Low priority through exec wrappers resolved on PATH: nice -n 10, plus taskpolicy -c utility on macOS, applied only when the program itself resolves. lowPriority and verifySlot are DriveOptions that the CLI always sets, as it sets keepAwake
payload.over: os.setPriority on the child after spawn; taskpolicy -b (darwin background); defaulting both on in the library

payload.because: Per-turn cost scales with the context carried. A resumed thread re-reads its whole history on every turn. That is cheap only while the cache is warm, since cache reads cost a tenth of fresh input; a cold resume re-writes the whole prefix at the cache-write premium. A fresh session starts small but pays to rediscover. 1.1 shows both sides: session 032d1bdd peaked at 266k and failed verify, and the fresh retry 17c753a6 rebuilt to 157k. Resuming pays only for short, warm work on the same context. The rule is code, so sofar still makes zero model calls.
payload.chose: Thread model with a deterministic resume-or-refresh rule in the coordinator. A task's conversation is resumed (claude --resume / --fork-session, codex resume) only when the gap since its last turn is inside the prompt-cache TTL and the work left is short: a verify_failed fix, a merge-conflict fix, or a park whose wait resolved. Otherwise the task gets a fresh session with the 3.3 packet. The 3.7 levers cut what a resume costs.
payload.over: Always resuming a task's thread (the Claude Code Projects and Managed Agents workflow shape), or never resuming (today's fresh session per task)

payload.title: Peer hint: when 3.1 denies an edit or 3.3 delivers a lease notice, name the lane holding the region as a reachable Claude Code peer (its SendMessage name from ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json, through core/peers.ts), so the blocked session can ask it directly. sofar never sends. The hint appears only on a live lease collision; Codex, Cursor and cloud lanes get the record packet alone. Driven `claude -p` sessions already register as peers (verified 2026-10-10: sofar-df was the 1.2 session)

Thread model (D15): a task is a thread, not a session. A retry or a resumed park continues the task's own conversation when the coordinator's resume-or-refresh rule says it pays, else a fresh session takes the 3.3 packet. Each task has an inbox in the record (events addressed to the task id), which hooks deliver at the next tool or prompt boundary. A parked thread is woken only when what it waits on resolves (a lease freed, a dependency merged, CI failed in Phase 4)

Thread cost levers (D15). (a) Shared warm prefix: the session-start injection is byte-identical across lanes with per-session lines last, and lane starts are staggered so lanes 2..N read lane 1's cache. (b) Warm-cache scheduling: resume inside the cache TTL, else refresh. (c) Fork at a checkpoint: a retry forks from the end of exploration, not from the failed attempt. (d) A parked thread holds no process. (e) A batched inbox: an FYI packet waits for the next boundary and never wakes a thread. (f) A per-thread context ceiling that hands off instead of compacting

Measure threads against fresh sessions on the 1.1 fixture: tokens per task split into cache read, cache write and fresh input (from transcripts, never handoff.tokens, which carries the whole session's summed usage, r4-fixes note 01M4K3G1), rework sessions and wall-clock. Keep each 3.7 lever only where it lowers cost with no drop in tasks done or verify pass rate

payload.because: A dangling handle names a target that may not be written yet, and the write surfaces warn rather than refuse it on that reason. The prompt path cannot read another log, and a foreign wait still open is the common case, so counting it as held matches the driver for as long as it is open. A new stop reason would change the run_stopped schema and the Rust types for a note's worth of information.
payload.chose: 1.3 readiness: a queued task is ready when every waits_on handle resolves (SPEC §Links states; open, moved and dangling hold it). Home handles resolve from the fold; foreign handles from the links tier in the driver and `sofar next --ready`, and count as held on the fold-only hot path (statusline, prompt line, TS and Rust). A run whose queue holds only waiting tasks stops `closed` with a note naming each wait.
payload.over: Ready when nothing is `open` (letting a dangling target through), reading other logs on the prompt path, or a new run stop reason

payload.because: Env does not reach every resolver: Codex starts MCP servers with a whitelisted env, and the verify child would carry the var into the hermetic suite. A marker is read by every process in the lane, whichever host launched it, and costs two small reads, only in linked worktrees. Sparse checkout flips the operator's repo to extensions.worktreeConfig. A symlink is a tracked change that `git add -A` commits. branch-visibility D1 forbids writing another checkout's copy because write-through duplicates lines at merge and forks that copy's queue. A lane never writes or commits its own copy, so the run's checkout holds the only live one, the blackboard the goal names. The marker is per-worktree state like HEAD, never a hook or a ref (commit-attribution D20).
payload.chose: 2.1 lane record root: a per-worktree marker, `<lane gitdir>/sofar-record-checkout`, names the run's checkout. recordRoot (TS) and record_root (Rust) then look for `.sofar` there, path for path, and never in the lane's committed copy, with no fallback to it. In a marked checkout, `sofar check --staged` reads the lane's own index and refuses a commit that stages `.sofar/`, whatever the block-commits opt-in. branch-visibility D1 is scoped, not superseded.
payload.over: An env override (SOFAR_ROOT) the driver sets. Sparse-checking-out the lane without .sofar. Symlinking the lane's .sofar, which is drive.ts's current advice. Splitting rootDir into a record dir and a git checkout across the 61 `.sofar` derivations.

payload.text: 2.1 hand-off to 2.2. (1) In a lane, rootDir IS the run's checkout. So the git facts that hooks read from rootDir are the checkout's, not the lane's: SessionStart's Git line, the branch binding, and the Stop gate's git dirt. So far only `sofar check` splits record from tree (CheckIo.lane). 2.2 decides whether hooks need the same split. (2) The lane prompt must say: commit code only, never .sofar, because the coordinator commits the record in the run's checkout. A lane session running `git -C <checkout> commit` on the record is NOT refused, since pre-commit then runs in the checkout, not the lane. (3) A sofar older than D18 ignores the marker and would write the lane's stale copy. That includes the activated native core in ~/.local/share/sofar/core/current, which the hook shims prefer. 2.2 should launch lanes only with a core and CLI that know the marker. (4) Full suite at 2.1: 4316 pass. The only failure was the shim-latency pin at load 82 (SessionStart best 312-649 ms, every other shim inside budget, and they all share the new root path), per branch-visibility M1.

payload.because: The state dir is the repo's per-clone home outside the tree (state-dir.ts), so vitest, tsc and rg never see N copies and the operator's parent dir stays clean. Per-lane locks let runs of different initiatives share one warm pool without colliding. A path is machine-local and the record is shared, so only the count is recorded. The lockfile stamp is what makes the install happen once.
payload.chose: 2.2 lane pool: lanes are linked worktrees at `<state base>/<clone key>/lanes/lane-<k>`, created on first use, kept across runs and initiatives, each marked to serve the checkout's record (D18). A driver holds a flock per lane (`lane-<k>.lock`, the run lock's primitive) and skips lanes another driver holds. Deps: a setup command (`--lane-setup`, else npm ci / pnpm / yarn / bun from the checkout's lockfile) runs in a lane only when its stamp in the lane's gitdir (command + lockfile sha256) differs. `run_started.lanes` (integer ≥2) is recorded; a resume keeps the recorded count; `--lanes 1` takes today's code path with nothing recorded.
payload.over: A sibling `<repo>.lanes/` dir; lanes inside the checkout; one pool per initiative; recording lane paths on run_started; reinstalling deps every run.

payload.because: The checkout's branch is checked out under the operator's working tree and peers' edits (M5), so moving its ref would desync their index. Committing leftovers before the gate makes the verified tree exactly what lands, and a clean checkout of the base then reproduces its fingerprint for the closing sweep. A reopened task that keeps its own branch continues the earlier session's tree, as serial drive does.
payload.chose: 2.2 tasks as branches: a lanes run cuts a run base branch `sofar/<slug>/<run>` from the checkout's HEAD. Each task works on `sofar/<slug>/<run>-<task>`, cut from the run base, in the lane already holding it or else the next clean lane. On task_done the driver commits whatever the session left uncommitted (`.sofar` excluded) on the task branch, gates in the lane, and fast-forwards the run base by compare-and-swap. A landed branch that gets reopened is reset to the base first. Tasks still run one at a time (2.3 adds concurrency), and a branch that cannot fast-forward stops the run with an error note naming the branch (2.4 adds rebase). The stop line names the base for the operator to merge.
payload.over: Moving the checkout's own branch; leaving leftovers uncommitted; reset-to-base on every launch; launching lanes concurrently in 2.2.

payload.because: An in-flight lane's work is real and independent of the lane that fired the stop; killing it throws that away and leaves no handoff. Counting launches in flight is the only way --max-sessions stays a bound when N launch at once. The cost cap can only see what has been reported, so the overshoot is stated rather than hidden (session-driver D14 already scopes it to one driver).
payload.chose: 2.3 coordinator: a lanes run (≥2) runs one loop that, each pass, gives every free lane (no live session, not parked) the first ready task no lane holds — in the lane holding its branch, else the next clean free lane — and runs each lane's session → gate → land → handoff as its own job. --max-sessions counts launches in flight; --cost-cap sums every lane's reported cost and is checked before each launch, so up to N-1 running sessions may add to it after it is reached. A stop rule that fires (needs_user, exhausted verify, an unlandable branch, stalls, a budget) launches nothing more and DRAINS: lanes in flight finish, are gated and file their handoffs, then run_stopped; the first stop wins. ^C or --stop signals every live session. Stalls count consecutively in completion order across lanes. A task_done is not credited for a task another lane held during the session. Concurrent launches resolve by the transport's session id; the timestamp fallback sees sibling sessions as candidates and stays unresolved rather than guess (session-driver D3). `--lanes 1` keeps the serial loop.
payload.over: Killing in-flight lanes when a stop rule fires; N independent loops; counting only finished sessions against --max-sessions; folding rebase into 2.3 (a diverged branch still stops the run as error per D20 until 2.4's merge queue)

payload.because: The task asks that the statusline and interactive sessions see which lane holds which task; both read the fold, so the assignment has to be an event. One event with an optional task is the smallest schema that can also free a lane after an unresolved launch.
payload.chose: Each assignment is a new event, `lane_assigned {run, lane: integer ≥1, task?}` on envelope session cli: with task, the coordinator gave that lane that task; without, it freed the lane (a launch that resolved to no session files no handoff to free it). The fold keeps `run.assignments` [{lane, task, ts}], lane order, present only when non-empty: an assignment replaces the lane's and any other lane's hold on the same task, and ends at the handoff for its task, at run_stopped and at run_adopted (the old driver's lanes are gone). Excluded from drift like every driver event (commit-attribution D18). Where the record shows "the task in flight", a lanes run shows what its lanes hold, `L<k> <task>` joined by ", ": describeRun (the injected Driven line and sofar status), the statusline's drive segment, the prompt's drive line and the progress file's `task`.
payload.over: Recording lanes only in the progress file (not the record, invisible to other clones and to the injected digest); a separate lane_released event type; putting the lane on handoff (an unresolved launch files no handoff, so the lane would read held forever)

payload.because: M1: a usage-limited launch looks like an unresolved stall and two stop the run, though nothing is wrong with the work. The stream names the limit and its reset, so the wait is read from a fact, not guessed. Routes can send lanes to different agents, so one lane's limit is not assumed to be every lane's. The serial run's behaviour is pinned byte for byte by 2.2.
payload.chose: A rate-limited lane parks: the claude-code adapter reports a stream `rate_limit_event` whose status is `rejected` on SessionExit.rate_limit {type?, resets_at?}. On a lanes run that launch never counts as a stall; its lane takes no task until the reset the stream names (+30s), or for 5 minutes doubling to 60 per consecutive park when none is named, and the task goes back to the queue for other lanes. A session that registered before the limit still files its handoff. With every lane parked the run waits for the earliest reset, still honouring --stop and ^C. A serial run is unchanged (a limited launch still stalls).
payload.over: Stopping the run on a rate limit; parking every lane on one lane's limit; parking a serial run too; matching stderr prose

payload.text: A driven session cannot run an env-prefixed command (`FOLD_PARITY_RECORD=1 npx vitest …`, `env X=1 …`): it falls outside the run's Bash surface and waits on an approval nobody gives. That is how RENDER_PARITY_RECORD=1 recorded FP-26's render golden in drive-lanes 2.3.

payload.because: Concurrent lanes make divergence the common case, so the D20 stop fired on most second landings. A merge left in the lane is finished with only `git add` and `git commit`, which the floor already grants, and its state is a fact git keeps, so the prompt is right on every path (runTask, recover, a resumed run). Rebasing first keeps the base linear for 2.6's bisect; merging a branch that already holds a merge keeps the session's resolution instead of replaying the conflict. A distinct handoff reason is what 2.5's merge-conflict reopen rate is counted from.
payload.chose: 2.4 merge queue: landings run one at a time through a promise-chain queue in the driver. A branch that already contains the base fast-forwards as before, with no re-verify. A branch the base moved past is integrated in its own lane: rebased onto the base tip when it holds no merge commit, else (or when the rebase stops) merged with `git merge --no-edit`. Either way the gate runs again in the lane on the new tree, and a pass fast-forwards the base by compare-and-swap. A merge that stops on conflicts is LEFT IN PROGRESS in the lane: the task is reopened, the session's handoff is the new reason `merge_conflict` with the conflicting paths as its detail, and the lane's next session (the lane holds the branch, and its dirty tree keeps other tasks out) is told by the prompt, read from the lane's MERGE_HEAD and unmerged paths, to resolve, `git add` and `git commit`. A lane still holding unmerged paths at acceptance is never committed: that is a merge conflict again, with no gate. One task's merge_conflict handoffs in a run count against --max-verify-attempts and stop the run as stall when they reach it.
payload.over: Rebase-only with the conflict aborted and the session told to `git rebase` (git rebase is outside the protocol floor, permissions.ts DEFAULT_ALLOW, so a driven session cannot run it, and a rebase in progress detaches HEAD so no lane would hold the branch); keeping the conflict in the record only (a resumed run's recover path has no session to file a handoff for, so the next prompt would lack it); stopping the run on any divergence (D20, D21's stop-until-2.4); rebasing at every launch.

payload.because: The operator's later ruling ("its better to check at last right? yes") created 2.6, which specifies the same split with the piece 2.4 lacks: bisecting a full-gate failure to its task. A batch suite built here could fail with no task to reopen, and two verify tiers built in two tasks would drift. The clause was the plan's reading at creation, not the operator's words.
payload.chose: 2.4's "affected-tests verify per merge, full suite per batch" clause is carried by 2.6. In 2.4 a merge re-verifies through the one acceptance gate (the task's own verify command, else the run's, plus the decision checks that apply to its files), so when 2.6 tiers that gate (typecheck plus covering tests per task, full gate per phase and run end, bisect to pin a failure) every merge re-verify is tiered with it.

plan.goal: sofar drive runs N lanes in parallel with conflict-aware orchestration: ready-frontier scheduling, region leases at edit time, a serial merge queue and the record as the shared blackboard. Local worktrees first, then Claude Code cloud sessions. Each step is kept only where it beats serial drive on a fixture (no degradation, in percentages).

tasks.title: Lane fixture and serial baseline: a sandbox repo with 9 tasks (6 independent, 3 chained by waits_on, 3 editing one shared function), each with a verify command. Serial drive's wall-clock, tasks done, verify pass rate, tokens per task and conflicts are the bar every later step must beat

Load control so lanes do not saturate the machine: a verify semaphore (one full suite at a time), nice/taskpolicy for sessions and verify, process-group kill on verify timeout, a vitest maxWorkers cap (drive-load note 01M3PCDC, fixes 1-5)
Ready frontier: readyTasks honours waits_on (queuedTasks ignores it today, drive-queue.ts:42); `sofar next --ready`; serial drive takes the ready head
Record-root override: a lane session writes the main checkout's .sofar, never its worktree's stale committed copy; lanes never commit .sofar

`sofar drive --lanes N`: a persistent lane worktree pool (deps installed once), tasks as branches, lanes recorded on run_started. `--lanes 1` stays byte-identical to today's run (session-driver D6 holds there)

Coordinator: one process assigns ready tasks to free lanes and records each assignment, so the statusline and interactive sessions see which lane holds which task. Budgets (--cost-cap, --max-sessions) count across lanes; a rate-limited lane parks instead of stalling

Serial merge queue: rebase a passing task branch onto the run base, re-verify when the base moved, fast-forward. A conflict becomes a merge handoff to the lane's next session. Affected-tests verify per merge, full suite per batch

Measure local lanes against serial on the 1.1 fixture. Keep only if wall-clock falls ≥40%, duplicate work is 0, tasks done and verify pass rate are no lower, merge-conflict reopens ≤10% and tokens per task rise ≤5%

Tiered verify: after each task run the typecheck plus the tests covering the files the task changed; run the full gate (whole vitest + cargo) once at a phase end and at the run end, and pin a full-gate failure to its task by bisecting the phase's task commits. Keep only if it beats per-task full verify on the 1.1 fixture with no failure missed.
A verify that times out re-runs the verify once load control (1.2) clears, never a new session; only a verify that fails charges the task.

Region leases at PreToolUse: an Edit's old_string maps to its markdown section or enclosing symbol, else the whole file. An overlap with another lane steers rather than denies, so r4-fixes D17 holds: the hook's context names the holding lane, its task, the region and what is free, and the session works elsewhere or parks (WIP commit, write-back, leases released). Older task wins, so no deadlock; union-merge files never lease. A deny mode sits behind a flag, off, until the operator rules on D17 for driven lanes

Footprint prediction and conflict-aware scheduling: task `touches`, the record's mention index, files earlier sessions on the task touched, git co-change. A free lane takes the first ready task that misses every live lease and footprint, else idles; skipped tasks age up

Context packets, deterministic and one line each: lease notice (who holds what, for which task), change brief on merge (task, regions, diffstat, decisions and memories logged, write-back), park/resume packet (own write-back, WIP sha, the brief it waited for)
Measure conflict-aware lanes against naive lanes: merge-conflict rework sessions, parks, lanes busy, wall-clock. Keep each piece only if it improves on 2.5

Peer hint: when 3.1 steers an edit away or 3.3 delivers a lease notice, name the lane holding the region as a reachable Claude Code peer (its SendMessage name from ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json, through core/peers.ts), so the blocked session can ask it directly. sofar never sends. The hint appears only on a live lease collision; Codex, Cursor and cloud lanes get the record packet alone. Driven `claude -p` sessions already register as peers (verified 2026-10-10: sofar-df was the 1.2 session)

Thread model (D15): a task is a thread, not a session. A retry or a resumed park continues the task's own conversation when the coordinator's resume-or-refresh rule says it pays, else a fresh session takes the 3.3 packet. Each task has an inbox in the record (events addressed to the task id), which hooks deliver at the next tool or prompt boundary. A parked thread is woken only when what it waits on resolves (a lease freed, a dependency merged, CI failed in Phase 4)

Thread cost levers (D15). (a) Shared warm prefix: the session-start injection is byte-identical across lanes with per-session lines last, and lane starts are staggered so lanes 2..N read lane 1's cache. (b) Warm-cache scheduling: resume inside the cache TTL, else refresh. (c) Fork at a checkpoint: a retry forks from the end of exploration, not from the failed attempt. (d) A parked thread holds no process. (e) A batched inbox: an FYI packet waits for the next boundary and never wakes a thread. (f) A per-thread context ceiling that hands off instead of compacting

Measure threads against fresh sessions on the 1.1 fixture: tokens per task split into cache read, cache write and fresh input (from transcripts, never handoff.tokens, which carries the whole session's summed usage, r4-fixes note 01M4K3G1), rework sessions and wall-clock. Keep each 3.7 lever only where it lowers cost with no drop in tasks done or verify pass rate

Add `--arm native` to the fixture harness: one Claude Code session drives all 9 fixture tasks with its own subagents, scored on tokens per task split into cache read, cache write and fresh input, tasks done and wall-clock. Then project from the 2.5 reps' transcripts what each retry and park would cost as a warm resume, a cold resume, a checkpoint fork and a fresh 3.3-packet session. 3.6-3.8 go ahead only for the cases where the projection beats both fresh sessions and the native arm; otherwise drop them, citing the numbers

Cloud launch and readback without a TTY: `claude --cloud` refuses a non-TTY (r4-fixes M24). Verify a scriptable launch (routines via API call, or a pty), a branch per task, results back through pushed branches (needs the Claude GitHub App on the repo), and session end detected from the branch's record

Cloud lane adapter: a lane is a cloud session on its task branch. The local coordinator polls and fetches, verifies locally, merges through the queue, and `--resume` re-attaches after the laptop sleeps (the record is the queue)
Conflicts in cloud lanes: no edit-time leases (a cloud VM cannot read the local lease store), so scheduling by footprint plus the merge queue. Measure conflict rework against local lanes
Measure cloud lanes against local lanes: wall-clock, cost per task, tasks finished with the laptop closed, verify pass rate

payload.because: The arms differ only in what the driver runs after a session, so agents add noise and cost and nothing else: 2.5's reps swung 410–1290 s on host load, while the fixture's whole gate costs ~0.1 s. As written, the fixture's full suite is red until all nine tasks are done, so per-task full verify cannot run on it at all; shipping each spec with its task makes `node --test` green after every correct task, which is the property a full gate has here. The replay is deterministic, so 'no failure missed' is checked exactly: every fault's task reopened, the final tree green.
payload.chose: 2.6 measures tiered verify on a REPLAY of the 1.1 fixture's nine tasks: the reference solutions as scripted sessions through the real driver and real gate commands, each spec test shipped with its task (as this repo ships tests), the plan in three phases, run-level gates (`node --test` full, `node scripts/related.mjs {files}` quick), three injected faults (1.5/1.6 overwrite formatPrice; 1.2 adds a module the README test reads from disk, which no import reaches), and a clean scenario; arms interleaved, 3 reps (test-e2e/drive-lanes/tiered-replay.test.ts → results/2.6-replay.json)
payload.over: Agent reps of the 1.1 fixture per D7 (`node run.mjs`), or the fixture as written (spec tests in the skeleton, a plan verify per task)

payload.because: The operator states both commands, so no runner table is guessed. One record per execution, against the task whose tree it checked, keeps the fold's per-task attempt counting honest. A serial run's checkout is shared with peers (M5), so a probe can only run in its own worktree; the lane pool already gives one with dependencies installed once. That is an exception to session-driver D6 for tiered runs only: without --verify-quick, --lanes 1 stays byte-identical. The coordinator's loop knows held tasks and busy lanes, and inside the merge queue no landing moves the base under the gate.
payload.chose: 2.6 tiered verify is opt-in through `--verify-quick <cmd>` (recorded as run_started.verify_quick, needs --verify; a resume keeps its own). A task with no verify of its own is gated on it, `{files}` = the paths the task touched, holds uncommitted or committed since its launch (since the run base on lanes), single-quoted; at the touched-list cap it runs --verify. --verify runs once when every task of a phase is resolved and one is in the window (tasks whose latest own pass came after the last --verify pass), and at the closing sweep; a pass on the exact tree covers the quick-tier checks there. A failure is bisected over the window's task commits (HEAD of each task's latest pass when the tree was clean), each probe in a clean lane recorded against the task whose commit it ran on, and the task owning the first failing commit is reopened. A serial tiered run claims one lane from the pool for the bisect, the first time it needs one.
payload.over: Deriving the quick tier from a built-in runner table (session-driver D8); recording the full gate once per window task; bisecting in the operator's checkout, or in a fresh worktree per probe; a phase-end gate built into runTask, where a lanes run cannot see which lanes are busy

payload.because: The replay's sessions cost nothing, so its wall-clock is the driver's bookkeeping alone; an agent rep of the same fixture spends ~622 s (2.5 serial mean) in sessions, against which 0.1-0.6 s is under 0.1%. On this repo's gate the saving is real: --verify averaged 220.7 s over 51 recorded runs; the quick tier measured 0.7 s typecheck plus 27-50 s of vitest related on real task file sets (-77% to -87% per task), and the closing sweep that ran the full gate 14 times on one tree (linked-context 01M3Q218) runs it once. results/2.6-replay.json, results/2.6-real-gate.json
payload.chose: 2.6 verdict keep, as opt-in `--verify-quick`: on the 1.1 fixture replay (D29, 3 interleaved reps) tiered verify misses no failure — all 3 faults reopened in both arms, every final tree green, the full-gate-only fault bisected to 1.2 in 2 probes — and runs the full suite 6 times to 20 (-70%) with faults, 3 to 17 (-82%) clean; gate seconds -8.9% / -23.8%. Defaults are unchanged: a run without --verify-quick gates exactly as before.
payload.over: Dropping it on the replay's wall-clock: +0.61 s (+21.6%) with faults, +0.12 s (+5.1%) clean, from extra git calls per task and, with faults, creating the serial bisect lane once

payload.text: To commit only your hunks of a file a peer's uncommitted work also touches: split `git diff -U0 -- <file>` into hunks, keep yours, `git apply --cached --unidiff-zero <patch>`, check `git diff --cached`, then plain `git commit -F <msg>` with NO pathspec — `git commit -- <path>` is --only mode and commits the worktree copy, peer hunks included. schema-fingerprint.txt is one line per event type, so it splits by hunk the same way. drive-lanes 2.6 did this with node_modules/.cache/stage26.mjs.

2.6 for the operator: to use tiered verify on this repo's drive runs, add --verify-quick "npm run -s typecheck && npx vitest related --run --project unit --passWithNoTests {files}" next to the existing --verify. Measured quick tier: 0.7 s typecheck + 27-50 s of vitest related against the 220.7 s full gate (51 runs). A schema change reaches 203 unit files, so its quick tier is most of the suite. A serial tiered run claims one pool lane for its bisect the first time a full gate fails; setup is --lane-setup or the lockfile's installer.

2.6 replay overhead: tiered adds ~40-50 ms per task of git calls (changed-file listing, launch HEAD) plus a one-time lane creation when a serial run first bisects. That is +0.12 s clean / +0.61 s faulted on a 3 s replay whose sessions cost nothing. Merging changedPaths and committedSince into one diff would trim a spawn per task if it ever matters.

payload.because: The operator ruled 2.7 from r4-fixes note 01M4K8J8: a timeout under load (81 on 14 cores) bought a whole session. (a) breaks D10: an unattended run must have no state it can sit in forever. (b) is what the operator ruled out: only a fail charges, never a new session. (c) lets dependents and lanes build on unverified, unlanded work. (d) is a schema change across TS, Rust and conformance for what `stall` already says. A second timeout after the load wait is no longer evidence of load, and only the operator can tell a hang from a bound set too tight, so a stop puts it in front of them without spending a session. A stopped run cannot be resumed, and recover only checked its own done tasks, so without the cross-run rule the task would stay done and unverified forever. Lanes are excluded because a new lanes base does not hold the stopped run's task branch.
payload.chose: 2.7: a verify timeout is never charged — failuresSoFar skips it, nothing is reopened, no session launched. The command runs once more after a load wait (`loadWait`, on in the CLI): the 1-minute load average below the core count, polled every 5 s, bounded by the command's own timeout and then re-run with a warning, with the verify slot not held while waiting. A re-run that times out too stops the run as `stall`, the task left done and unaccepted (unlanded on lanes, the note names its branch). The full gate and its bisect probes stop the same way. A done task whose newest check is a timeout counts as unchecked, so the next serial run, new or resumed, gates it first. The stall note now counts failures, not attempts.
payload.over: (a) Re-running until a verdict with no bound; (b) after N timeouts, charging a timeout as a fail and reopening; (c) leaving the timed-out task unaccepted while the run carries on; (d) a new run stop reason

payload.because: Only a driven lane can collide with another lane, so only a lane session should pay for the check, and the driver already writes each session's settings file (2.4, D8). Files beside the lane locks need no fold and no record read on the edit path, and the lock tells a dead driver's leftover lease from a live one. Names are what two copies of a file share. Wound-wait ordering is what makes "older task wins" a no-deadlock guarantee rather than a tie-break.
payload.chose: 3.1 region leases, built as: a lanes run gives each lane session a PreToolUse hook (matcher Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit) through that session's own --settings file, running `sofar event lease` on the TypeScript engine only (sofar-core answers exit 64, as for drive-await; rust-core D15/D16 scoped, not superseded: the core owns no new shape). Leases are per-lane append-only files beside the lane locks, `<pool>/lane-<k>.lease.jsonl`: the coordinator writes the header (run, task, title, first assignment time, mode) when it assigns the lane and deletes the file when the job ends, after gate and landing; the hook appends claims and waits; a lease counts only while its lane lock is held. A region is the deepest markdown section or code symbol (indentation outline plus declaration patterns) holding the edit's old_string, its own lines or with its children; Write, NotebookEdit and other file types take the whole file; `.sofar/` and merge=union paths never lease. Two regions overlap on the same name, on an ancestor that holds its children, or on the whole file. The older task (first assignment in the run, then lane number) wins, so a session is steered or denied only by an older holder and the wait-for graph has no cycle. Steer is additionalContext with no permissionDecision, so the edit applies and r4-fixes D17 holds; `--leases deny` returns permissionDecision deny (D14); `--leases off` is 3.4's naive arm; default steer, a per-driver knob that is not recorded. A session that ends with no task change after a steer has parked: its handoff stays `stall` with detail `parked on a lease …`, is not counted toward --max-stalls, and its task is held out of the ready set until every holder's lease is gone, then its branch integrates the base before the relaunch.
payload.over: Widening the project PreToolUse matcher (every interactive edit of every sofar user would pay a hook spawn, a node boot where no native core is installed). Porting the lease logic to sofar-core too (two implementations of a driven-only path). Leases as record events (an event per edit, for state that is machine-local coordination; cloud lanes cannot read it either, 4.3). Line-range regions (each lane edits its own copy, so line ranges drift while names hold). A new `parked` handoff reason (a schema change while packages/schema/src is mid-edit by a peer session). First holder wins (two lanes each parked on the other's region livelock).

payload.because: The operator asked that once lane 1 finishes, the driver share it with lane 2 so lane 2 can write that file, and share context between lanes and the records — efficient and pre-engineered (brief 2026-10-10). Rendering from held facts keeps sofar at zero model calls and makes each packet byte-stable. Gating each delivery on relevance (the file being edited, the merge taking the landing in, the task coming back) means a lane pays roughly 100–400 tokens only where a packet bears on its next move, and the briefs cite D/M ids and write-backs that live in the record. 3.4 measures the whole conflict-aware arm against naive lanes.
payload.chose: 3.3 context packets, built as: three one-line packets rendered by core/packets.ts from facts already held (lease files, git, the fold), never a model, bounded (brief 800, notice 800, resume 1,600 chars), on a lanes run that leases only — `--leases off`, 3.4's naive arm, delivers none. LEASE NOTICE: in a lane session's opening prompt, every live lease another lane holds regions under; and at the lease hook, once per older holder and file, when an edit met none of that holder's regions (a steer in that file already named it otherwise). CHANGE BRIEF: read at each landing (git numstat, -U0 hunks mapped to the landed copy's sections and symbols by regions.ts spanRegions, one cat-file --batch), the D/M the task's sessions in this run logged (event ids by envelope session, numbered by fold position), the landing session's write-back; kept in the driver and appended to every other lease this run holds — the lease file doubles as the lane's inbox, opened without O_CREAT — said by that lane's hook once at its first edit of a file the landing changed; and listed under a conflicted merge's prompt for the landings it takes in (latest 3), as the other side's intent. RESUME PACKET: opens a lane session whose task a session of this run already handed off (park, failed check, merge conflict, stall): that session, how it ended, its write-back, the WIP (head, commits past the base, uncommitted paths), and after a park each waited lease's holder brief when it landed after the parked session launched, else that it let go.
payload.over: Packets as record events (a schema change for something git and the record can re-derive; how cloud lanes, which cannot read the pool, get them is 4.3's to decide). A second per-lane inbox file (the lease already has exactly that lifetime and is already read on every edit). Regions from lease claims (what was claimed, not what landed, and nothing at all under --leases off). Every brief to every lane at its next tool call (tokens spent on files it never touches). Packets in the naive arm (would blur 3.4's comparison). A resume packet for parks only (a failed-check or merge-conflict retry would rediscover what the last session knew — D15's fresh-session-with-packet case).

No hint on a repeat collision, the launch notice, or any session absent from the registry (Codex, Cursor, cloud, ended).
payload.over: The session id in the lease header (the coordinator writes it before the session exists, and a relaunch changes it). A hint in the launch notice (no collision yet, tokens on lanes it may never touch). Gating on the hook adapter alone (the registry check names Codex/Cursor/cloud on both sides without knowing the adapter). sofar posting to the peer socket (peers.ts: addressing layer only).

LOWER, the thread's best case: it skips the retry's calls before its first edit and resumes on the 3.3 packet alone (400 tokens). UPPER: it replays every retry call on its larger base and resumes with the retry's own session-start tail. A lever (warm resume, cold resume, checkpoint fork) goes ahead for a kind of case only if, at both bounds, it is below both fresh sessions (plain and 3.3-packet) on raw tokens and on price, and every arm holding such cases, run that way at the lower bound, is below the native arm per task on both.

The cell has no sofar init, so no record, no hooks and an empty strict MCP config. It runs on D6's stack and D27's profile, with the driven surface minus sofar's rules and 9 × the session timeout. payload.because: Threads only act on retries and parks, and the kept default (footprint scheduling, D37) has none. Where retries do exist, a thread wins only if it skips the retry's whole rediscovery, and even then the arm stays above native. The gap to native is per session, not per retry (results/3.9-thread-gate.json `shape`). A driven session starts at 29.6k context and makes 9.4 calls per task at a mean context of 33.2k. A native subagent starts at 15.4k and makes 4.4 calls per task at 18.2k, plus 2.5 main-thread calls per task at 47.9k. To close the gap, cut a driven session's base context and its per-task calls; resuming threads does neither. That is an operator call, outside this plan's tasks.

payload.chose: 3.10 integrate at edit: on a lanes run that leases, the lane's lease hook, at its first edit of a file a landing changed after the lane's branch was cut (an unsaid 3.3 brief naming the file, its landing tip not in HEAD), merges the newest landing this lane was told of into its branch, by fast-forward when the branch has no commits of its own, else a merge commit, but only when nothing the lane changed (commits past the merge base, uncommitted and untracked paths, .sofar excluded) meets a file the base changed, and never over a merge or rebase already in progress. Having moved the file under the edit, it refuses that one edit (permissionDecision deny, in steer mode too) with the brief and "read it again and redo the edit on top". Where the lane's changes meet the landing, it touches nothing and says the brief, as in 3.3. This extends D14's driven-lane exception to r4-fixes D17 to this one stale-edit refusal; interactive sessions keep D17 in full.
payload.over: Leaving the landing to the merge queue (both 3.4 conflicts were exactly this: the holder landed, its lease ended, and a lane cut before that landing edited formatPrice unsteered, then conflicted at its own landing after hand-copying 1.4's logic, as the brief's "build on it" invited). Letting the edit through after the merge (a Write made against the old text would revert the landing silently). The driver merging into live lanes at each landing (it would move files under an agent at a moment unrelated to what it edits). plan.goal: sofar drive runs N lanes in parallel with conflict-aware orchestration: ready-frontier scheduling, region leases at edit time, a serial merge queue and the record as the shared blackboard. Local worktrees first, then Claude Code cloud sessions. Each step is kept only where it beats serial drive on a fixture (no degradation, in percentages), and a driven task costs fewer tokens than native Claude Code (one session with its own subagents) on the same fixture.

tasks.title: Lane fixture and serial baseline: a sandbox repo with 9 tasks (6 independent, 3 chained by waits_on, 3 editing one shared function), each with a verify command. Serial drive's wall-clock, tasks done, verify pass rate, tokens per task and conflicts are the bar every later step must beat

Load control so lanes do not saturate the machine: a verify semaphore (one full suite at a time), nice/taskpolicy for sessions and verify, process-group kill on verify timeout, a vitest maxWorkers cap (drive-load note 01M3PCDC, fixes 1-5)
Ready frontier: readyTasks honours waits_on (queuedTasks ignores it today, drive-queue.ts:42); `sofar next --ready`; serial drive takes the ready head
Record-root override: a lane session writes the main checkout's .sofar, never its worktree's stale committed copy; lanes never commit .sofar

`sofar drive --lanes N`: a persistent lane worktree pool (deps installed once), tasks as branches, lanes recorded on run_started. `--lanes 1` stays byte-identical to today's run (session-driver D6 holds there)

Coordinator: one process assigns ready tasks to free lanes and records each assignment, so the statusline and interactive sessions see which lane holds which task. Budgets (--cost-cap, --max-sessions) count across lanes; a rate-limited lane parks instead of stalling

Serial merge queue: rebase a passing task branch onto the run base, re-verify when the base moved, fast-forward. A conflict becomes a merge handoff to the lane's next session. Affected-tests verify per merge, full suite per batch

Measure local lanes against serial on the 1.1 fixture. Keep only if wall-clock falls ≥40%, duplicate work is 0, tasks done and verify pass rate are no lower, merge-conflict reopens ≤10% and tokens per task rise ≤5%

Tiered verify: after each task run the typecheck plus the tests covering the files the task changed; run the full gate (whole vitest + cargo) once at a phase end and at the run end, and pin a full-gate failure to its task by bisecting the phase's task commits. Keep only if it beats per-task full verify on the 1.1 fixture with no failure missed.
A verify that times out re-runs the verify once load control (1.2) clears, never a new session; only a verify that fails charges the task.

Region leases at PreToolUse: an Edit's old_string maps to its markdown section or enclosing symbol, else the whole file. An overlap with another lane steers rather than denies, so r4-fixes D17 holds: the hook's context names the holding lane, its task, the region and what is free, and the session works elsewhere or parks (WIP commit, write-back, leases released). Older task wins, so no deadlock; union-merge files never lease. A deny mode sits behind a flag, off, until the operator rules on D17 for driven lanes

Footprint prediction and conflict-aware scheduling: task `touches`, the record's mention index, files earlier sessions on the task touched, git co-change. A free lane takes the first ready task that misses every live lease and footprint, else idles; skipped tasks age up

Context packets, deterministic and one line each: lease notice (who holds what, for which task), change brief on merge (task, regions, diffstat, decisions and memories logged, write-back), park/resume packet (own write-back, WIP sha, the brief it waited for)
Measure conflict-aware lanes against naive lanes: merge-conflict rework sessions, parks, lanes busy, wall-clock. Keep each piece only if it improves on 2.5

Peer hint: when 3.1 steers an edit away or 3.3 delivers a lease notice, name the lane holding the region as a reachable Claude Code peer (its SendMessage name from ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json, through core/peers.ts), so the blocked session can ask it directly. sofar never sends. The hint appears only on a live lease collision; Codex, Cursor and cloud lanes get the record packet alone. Driven `claude -p` sessions already register as peers (verified 2026-10-10: sofar-df was the 1.2 session)

Thread model (D15): a task is a thread, not a session. A retry or a resumed park continues the task's own conversation when the coordinator's resume-or-refresh rule says it pays, else a fresh session takes the 3.3 packet. Each task has an inbox in the record (events addressed to the task id), which hooks deliver at the next tool or prompt boundary. A parked thread is woken only when what it waits on resolves (a lease freed, a dependency merged, CI failed in Phase 4)

Thread cost levers (D15). (a) Shared warm prefix: the session-start injection is byte-identical across lanes with per-session lines last, and lane starts are staggered so lanes 2..N read lane 1's cache. (b) Warm-cache scheduling: resume inside the cache TTL, else refresh. (c) Fork at a checkpoint: a retry forks from the end of exploration, not from the failed attempt. (d) A parked thread holds no process. (e) A batched inbox: an FYI packet waits for the next boundary and never wakes a thread. (f) A per-thread context ceiling that hands off instead of compacting

Measure threads against fresh sessions on the 1.1 fixture: tokens per task split into cache read, cache write and fresh input (from transcripts, never handoff.tokens, which carries the whole session's summed usage, r4-fixes note 01M4K3G1), rework sessions and wall-clock. Keep each 3.7 lever only where it lowers cost with no drop in tasks done or verify pass rate

Thread gate, before any thread code (operator 2026-10-11: build threads only once proven efficient; they must save tokens against native workflows). Add `--arm native` to the fixture harness: one Claude Code session drives all 9 fixture tasks with its own subagents, scored on tokens per task split into cache read, cache write and fresh input, tasks done and wall-clock. Then project from the 2.5 reps' transcripts what each retry and park would cost as a warm resume, a cold resume, a checkpoint fork and a fresh 3.3-packet session. 3.6-3.8 go ahead only for the cases where the projection beats both fresh sessions and the native arm; otherwise drop them, citing the numbers

A lane session steered or denied by a lease that sets its task blocked on the holding lane's task is a park, not needs_user: in all 3 of 3.4's leasing reps the agent did that and stopped the run (D37). Close the younger-claims-first gap too (2 of 3 still conflicted). Then re-measure steer against footprint alone on a fixture pair whose footprints miss (a hub both edit outside their titles) before leases can return as a default

Token anatomy, deterministic, from the 3.4 and 3.9 transcripts: split a driven session's and a native subagent's tokens by source (system prompt and tool schemas, built-in and MCP; the SessionStart injection; each hook's added context; sofar protocol calls and their results; the task's own work; verify runs). results/4.1-anatomy.json ranks the sources by tokens per task and names what 4.2-4.4 must cut to land under native (driven today: 29.6k base, 9.4 calls per task; native subagent: 15.4k, 4.4)

Lean driven base: a driven session starts at or under a native subagent's base context. The driver hands a task packet (the task, its verify, the decisions and memories that name its files) instead of the full SessionStart digest; per-tool hook context is off in driven sessions unless it carries a rule the edit breaks; the MCP tool list is trimmed to what a driven session calls. Keep only if tasks done and gate pass rate hold

Bookkeeping by the driver, not the session: the driver records session start, task status and the write-back from what it already sees (the launch, the commit, its own verify, the session's last message), so a driven session spends no calls on the protocol; the prompt names the verify command so the session runs it once before it ends. Target at most 4.4 calls per task

Cache-shaped launches: every driven session in a run starts on a byte-identical prefix (system, tools, packet frame) with per-task lines last, so session N reads session N-1's cache inside the TTL, and lanes stagger their starts so lanes 2..N read lane 1's. Measure cache write per task against native's 11.8k

Measure serial and footprint lanes with 4.2-4.4 against native, 3 interleaved reps each on D27's stack. Keep each lever only where it lowers tokens per task (raw and priced) with no drop in tasks done or gate pass. The phase is done only when serial drive sits below native on tokens per task; otherwise name the remaining gap and the next lever as a task

Cloud launch and readback without a TTY: `claude --cloud` refuses a non-TTY (r4-fixes M24). Verify a scriptable launch (routines via API call, or a pty), a branch per task, results back through pushed branches (needs the Claude GitHub App on the repo), and session end detected from the branch's record

Cloud lane adapter: a lane is a cloud session on its task branch. The local coordinator polls and fetches, verifies locally, merges through the queue, and `--resume` re-attaches after the laptop sleeps (the record is the queue)
Conflicts in cloud lanes: no edit-time leases (a cloud VM cannot read the local lease store), so scheduling by footprint plus the merge queue. Measure conflict rework against local lanes
Measure cloud lanes against local lanes: wall-clock, cost per task, tasks finished with the laptop closed, verify pass rate

          'the same way — done and committed — until sofar tells you the context',
          'is nearly full. That message names a percentage and asks you to finish the',
          'current task and hand off; when it arrives, finish that task and end your turn',
          'without starting another. Your closing block lists every task you finished.',
        ]
      : [
          'Do THIS TASK ONLY, to the acceptance criteria the record names. Do not start the',
          'next one: the driver launches a fresh session for it, and running on costs the',
          'context that session needs.',
        ]
  return [
    `You are one session in a driven run of the initiative \\`${initiative}\\`. Your task is`,
    'named in the prompt. The record — goal, standing constraints, decisions, next action —',
    `is injected at session start; if you did not receive it, run \\`sofar status ${initiative}\\``,
    'before anything else.',
    '',

          'branch of its own. Work and commit there; the driver lands the branch once the',
          'task is accepted. The record is the run checkout\\'s: sofar reads and writes it from',

    'final reply with one fenced block whose info string is sofar, holding JSON, with',
    'your task\\'s id:',
    '',
    '```sofar',
    '{"summary":"<what you did, one or two sentences>","next_action":"<the next step>","tasks":[{"task_id":"<your task\\'s id>","status":"done"}]}',
